facts.statement: The species H. reticulatus and H. hauffianus are known from the Early Jurassic of Europe.
facts.quote: both known from the Early Jurassic of Europe

facts.statement: A preserved specimen of Hybodus hauffianus was found with over 100 belemnite rostra in its stomach.
facts.quote: A preserved specimen of Hybodus hauffianus has been found with over 100 belemnite (a type of extinct squid-like cephalopod) rostra (hard mineralized internal elements) in its stomach

facts.statement: With current knowledge, Hybodus is considered endemic to the Jurassic period.
facts.quote: con los conocimientos actuales Hybodus es una especie endemica del Jurásico

facts.statement: Several species previously assigned to Hybodus from the Cretaceous have been transferred to the genus Meristodonoides.
facts.quote: Varias especies del Cretácico se han trasladado a Meristodonoides

facts.statement: Some Triassic species previously assigned to Hybodus are not hybodonts and belong to the order Synechodontiformes.
facts.quote: Algunas especies del Triásico ni siquiera son hibodontos y forman parte de los Synechodontiformes

facts.statement: Hybodus possessed two dorsal fins that helped it aim at its prey with precision.
facts.quote: Poseía dos aletas dorsales que le ayudaban a dirigirse a su presa con precisión

facts.statement: Hybodus had two different types of teeth, suggesting a varied diet.
facts.quote: En primer lugar, tenían dos tipos diferentes de dientes, lo que sugiere una dieta variada

facts.statement: Sharper teeth were used to catch slippery prey, while flatter teeth likely helped crush shelled animals.
facts.quote: Los dientes más afilados se utilizarían para atrapar a presas resbaladizas, mientras que los dientes más planos probablemente les ayudaba a aplastar a los animales con caparazón

facts.statement: Hybodus had a bony plate on its dorsal fin, which likely had a defensive function.
facts.quote: En segundo lugar, tenían una lámina ósea en su aleta dorsal, que probablemente tenía una función defensiva

facts.statement: Males possessed pterigopodia, specialized organs that directly insert sperm into the female during mating.
facts.quote: Los machos poseen pterigopodios, órganos especializados que insertan directamente el esperma en la hembra durante el apareamiento

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database records Hybodus occurrences from the Gzhelian to the Maastrichtian (303.7 to 66 million years ago).
facts.quote: Time range: Gzhelian to Maastrichtian (303.7 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Hybodus belongs to the parent group Hybodontinae.
Hybodus is classified in the family Hybodontidae.
Hybodus is classified in the class Chondrichthyes.
